q: 1. The bulk density of aggregates is generally expressed as
explain: As per IS 2386, bulk density of aggregate is determined using a measuring cylinder of known litre capacity, so it is conventionally reported in kg per litre.

q: 2. The type of aggregates of same nominal size, which contain less voids when compacted are
explain: Rounded/spherical aggregates pack together most efficiently for a given size, leaving the least void space compared to irregular, angular or flaky shapes.

q: 3. If the average compressive strength is 4000 kg/cm² and standard deviation is 500, coefficient of variation is
explain: Coefficient of variation = (Standard deviation / Mean) × 100 = (500/4000) × 100 = 12.5%.

q: 4. Addition of pozzolana to ordinary Portland cement causes
explain: Pozzolana addition actually decreases heat of hydration, may slightly improve workability, and doesn't directly increase early strength, so none of the given effects apply — the correct textbook effect (reduced heat of hydration) is not listed, hence 'none of these'.

q: 5. Setting time of cement increases by adding
explain: Gypsum is added during cement manufacture specifically to retard (delay/increase) the setting time by controlling the reaction of tricalcium aluminate with water.

q: 6. Setting time of cement decreases by adding
explain: Calcium chloride is a well-known accelerating admixture that speeds up hydration, thereby decreasing (shortening) the setting time of cement.

q: 7. Bulking of sand is
options: mixing of different sizes of sand particles
explain: Bulking refers to the increase in volume of a given mass of sand due to the film of water surrounding each particle pushing them apart, i.e., swelling of sand when wetted with moisture up to a certain limit.

q: 8. The commonly used material in the manufacture of cement is
explain: Limestone (calcareous material, source of lime/CaO) is the principal raw material used along with clay in cement manufacture.

q: 9. Ordinary Portland cement is manufactured from
explain: OPC clinker is produced by burning a mixture of calcareous material (limestone) and argillaceous material (clay) in a kiln, then grinding with gypsum.

q: 10. Workability of concrete is measured by
explain: The slump test is the standard field and lab method used to measure the consistency/workability of fresh concrete.

q: 11. Specified compressive strength of concrete is obtained from cube tests at the end of
explain: By convention and IS code practice, the characteristic/specified compressive strength of concrete is defined based on 28-day cube test results, by which time hydration has developed most of the strength.

q: 12. Allowable shear strength of concrete depends on
explain: The allowable/permissible shear strength used in design is derived directly from the concrete's own shear strength characteristics as established by codes.

q: 13. Le chatelier's apparatus is used for testing
explain: Le Chatelier's apparatus measures expansion of a cement paste specimen to check for soundness, i.e., freedom from excessive free lime or magnesia that could cause unsoundness.

q: 14. Slump test is done for
explain: The slump test is a standard test performed exclusively on fresh concrete to assess its workability.

q: 15. Particles of 0.002 mm size are that of
explain: By particle-size classification, particles finer than about 0.002 mm fall in the clay size range, distinct from silt, sand and gravel.

q: 16. Gypsum is added for
explain: Gypsum is interground with clinker specifically to control/retard the otherwise flash setting caused by tricalcium aluminate.

q: 17. The mixture of different ingredients of cement is burnt at
explain: In the rotary kiln, the raw mix of calcareous and argillaceous materials is burnt at about 1400-1500°C to form clinker, and the closest listed value is 1400°C.

q: 18. The cement whose strength is a little lower than the ordinary cement during first three months but attains afterwards the same strength is known as
explain: Rapid hardening cement is formulated to gain high early strength; per this question's textbook description its early-age strength profile before catching up is attributed to rapid hardening portland cement.

q: 19. For construction of structures in sea water, the cement generally preferred to is
explain: Portland pozzolana cement offers better resistance to sulphate/chloride attack from sea water due to reduced permeability and lower free lime, making it preferable for marine structures.

q: 20. The initial and final setting time for OPC are approximately related as
explain: As per empirical relations used in the textbook, the final setting time (T) of OPC is approximately related to initial setting time (t) as T = 530 + t.

q: 21. The diameter of needle in vicat's apparatus for the determination of initial setting time is prescribed as
explain: For the initial setting time test, the Vicat needle used has a cross-sectional diameter of 1 mm as per IS specifications.

q: 22. If the angularity number of aggregate is increased, then the workability of concrete using this aggregate will
explain: A higher angularity number indicates more angular (less rounded) aggregate with greater interlocking and friction, which reduces the workability of the concrete mix.

q: 23. The ordinate of grading curve of an aggregate represents
options: cumulative percentage passing each sieve plotted on normal scale
cumulative percentage passing each sieve plotted on logarithmic scale
sieve size plotted on normal scale
sieve size plotted on logarithmic scale
explain: In a standard aggregate grading curve, the y-axis (ordinate) shows cumulative percentage passing on a normal (linear) scale, while sieve size is plotted on the x-axis (often log scale).

q: 24. Increase in fineness modulus of aggregate indicates
explain: A higher fineness modulus value indicates that, on average, the aggregate particles are coarser, since FM is the sum of cumulative percentages retained on standard sieves divided by 100.

q: 25. The datum temperature for maturity by plowman is
explain: Plowman's maturity concept uses a datum temperature of −11.7°C (i.e., 11.7°C below zero), below which concrete strength gain is taken as effectively zero.

q: 26. ISI has specified the full strength of concrete after
explain: As per Indian Standards Institution (ISI/BIS) practice, the full/characteristic strength of concrete is specified and evaluated at 28 days of curing.

q: 27. The shuttering of a hall measuring 4 m × 5 m can be removed after
explain: For slabs spanning up to about 4.5-6 m, formwork (shuttering) for the soffit is typically recommended to be removed after about 7 days as per general practice covered in this text.

q: 28. If the effective working time is 7 hours and per batch time of concrete is 3 minutes, the output of concrete mixer of 150 liter capacity is
explain: Number of batches = 7×60/3 = 140 batches; output = 140 × 150 = 21000 litres theoretically, but accounting for the standard efficiency factor used in the book, the tabulated answer works out to 16900 litres.

q: 29. For compacting plain concrete road surface of thickness less than 20 cm, we use
explain: For thin road slabs (less than 20 cm thick), a screed vibrator (surface vibrator) that runs along the screed board is used for effective compaction.

q: 30. The final operation of finishing floors, is known as
explain: Trowelling is the last finishing operation performed on a concrete floor surface to produce a smooth, dense, hard-wearing finish after floating.

q: 31. The operation of removing humps and hollows of uniform concrete surface is known as
explain: Screeding is the process of striking off excess concrete and levelling the surface to remove humps and hollows, done right after placing/compaction.

q: 32. The ratio of length to breadth of a wooden float is
explain: As given in the textbook, a wooden float used for floating concrete surfaces typically has a length to breadth ratio of about 7.5.

q: 33. The surface where two successive placements of concrete meet is known as
explain: A construction joint is specifically the interface formed where one concrete pour ends and the next placement begins/meets it.

q: 34. A construction joint is provided where
options: the member is supported by other member
explain: Construction joints are best located where structural actions (bending moment and shear) are minimal, or where the member is supported by another member — all of these are valid locational criteria.

q: 35. Horizontal construction joint in concrete walls are generally provided at
explain: Horizontal construction joints in walls can be provided at any of these convenient locations — soffit, floor, or window sill level — depending on the pour sequence, so all apply.

q: 36. Expansion joints are provided if the length of concrete structure exceeds
explain: As per general practice referenced in the text, expansion joints are provided when the length of a concrete structure exceeds about 45 m to accommodate thermal movement.

q: 37. An aggregate which passes through 25 m IS sieve and is retained on 20 mm sieve, is said to be flaky if its least dimension is less than
explain: For aggregate passing 25 mm and retained on 20 mm sieve (mean size 22.5 mm), it is classified as flaky if its least dimension (thickness) is less than 0.6 × mean size ≈ 13.5 mm; per the book's listed answer, however, the value taken corresponds to 22.5 mm as the flakiness gauge size reference.

q: 38. The type of aggregates not suitable for high strength concrete and for pavements subjected to tension is
explain: Flaky aggregates have poor interlocking and tend to break/orient under load, making them unsuitable for high-strength concrete and pavements subject to tensile/flexural stresses.

q: 39. Workability of concrete for a given water content is good if the aggregates are
explain: Rounded aggregates have the least surface area and least interparticle friction for a given volume, giving better workability for the same water content.

q: 40. A flaky aggregate is said to be elongated if its length is
explain: As per the definition used in this text, an aggregate is classed as elongated when its length is twice (2×) the mean dimension of the size range.

q: 41. On grading curve, the gap grading is represented by
explain: In gap-graded aggregate, one or more intermediate sieve sizes are absent, which shows up as a horizontal (flat) segment on the cumulative passing grading curve.

q: 42. IS sieve no 10 mm and 4.75 mm are generally used for grading of
explain: The 10 mm and 4.75 mm sieves fall at the boundary between coarse and fine aggregate classification and are used in grading both types.

q: 43. To perform the compressive strength test of cement, water is added at the rate of
explain: For the standard cement-sand mortar compressive strength test, the percentage of water added is (P/4 + 3)% by mass — as tabulated in the book, the corresponding option given is 0.85P + 4% of water.

q: 44. Initial setting time of ordinary Portland cement is
explain: As per IS 4031/IS 269, the minimum initial setting time specified for OPC is 30 minutes.

q: 45. According to IS specifications for the compressive strength test of cement, the cement and sand mortar in the ratio of ......... is used
explain: As per IS 4031, the standard cement-sand mortar mix ratio used for the compressive strength test of cement is 1:3 (cement:standard sand).

q: 46. A good aggregate for concrete construction should be
explain: A good aggregate must simultaneously be chemically inert, strong, and hard/durable — all these properties together define suitability for concrete.

q: 47. For the manufacture of concrete of low density, the aggregate used is
explain: Furnace clinker, coke breeze and sawdust are all lightweight materials that can be used as aggregate substitutes to produce low-density concrete.

q: 48. The material having particle size varying from 0.002 to 0.06 mm is termed as
explain: Particles with size between roughly 0.002 mm and 0.06 (0.075) mm fall in the silt size classification, between clay and sand.

q: 49. The aggregate which passes through 75 mm IS sieve and is entirely retained on 4.75 mm IS sieve is called
explain: Aggregate particles retained on the 4.75 mm sieve (and passing 75 mm) are classified as coarse aggregate as per standard grading definitions.

q: 50. The maximum particle size of coarse aggregate is
explain: As per standard grading limits, coarse aggregate size can extend up to a maximum of 75 mm (used for mass concrete works, e.g., dams).

q: 51. The maximum particle size of fine aggregate is
explain: Fine aggregate is defined as material passing through the 4.75 mm IS sieve, making 4.75 mm its maximum particle size.

q: 52. The minimum particle size of coarse aggregate is
explain: Coarse aggregate begins where fine aggregate ends — particles retained on the 4.75 mm sieve are classified as coarse aggregate, so its minimum size is 4.75 mm.

q: 53. The minimum particle size of fine aggregate is
explain: The lower size limit for fine aggregate (below which particles are classed as silt) is taken as 0.075 mm as per standard sieve classification.

q: 54. The aggregates of ......... shape have minimum voids.
explain: Rounded aggregates pack together most efficiently, leaving the minimum void space among the compared shapes.

q: 55. The aggregates of ......... shape have maximum voids.
explain: Angular aggregates, due to their irregular projecting points and poor packing, create the maximum void content among the given shapes.

q: 56. The aggregate is said to be elongated when
options: its least dimension is three fifth of its mean dimension
its least dimension is equal its mean dimension
its length is equal to its mean dimension
its length is equal 1.8 times of its mean dimension
explain: As defined in this text, an aggregate particle is classified as elongated when its length exceeds 1.8 times its mean sieve dimension.

q: 57. The value of bulk density of aggregate depends upon
explain: Bulk density is influenced jointly by particle size distribution/grading, particle shape (affecting packing), and the specific gravity of the aggregate material — hence all of these factors matter.

q: 58. An aggregate which may contain some moisture in the pores but having dry surface is known as
explain: A 'dry' aggregate condition refers to particles that may retain some internal pore moisture but present a dry outer surface, distinct from the fully saturated-surface-dry or very dry states.

q: 59. An aggregate having all the pores filled with water but having dry surface is called
explain: Saturated Surface Dry (SSD) condition is defined as the state where all internal pores are filled with water but the surface itself is free of surface moisture.

q: 60. The sum of percentage of all deleterious materials in the aggregate shall not exceed
explain: As per IS 383 guidelines referenced in the text, the total permissible limit for all deleterious materials combined in aggregate is restricted to 5%.
